title: CTAB/Chloroform-Isoamyl Alcohol DNA Extraction Protocol
author: Elena L. Peredo
materials: Routinely, we use ethanol and bleach to clean working areas and surfaces. Wipe, wipe, wipe. Micro pestles need to be properly treated beforehand. DNA is thermostable, so it might not be completely degraded by autoclaving alone. The treatment involves using bleach (DNA is more unstable at low pH, leading to depurination, compared to high pH, which causes denaturation). Rinse multiple times in distilled water to remove any remnant of bleach. Additionally, using high-intensity UV, such as that provided by a crosslinker UV machine, is also desired.

steps.title: Wash algae cells to remove debris
steps.instruction: Allow the culture to settle in an Erlenmeyer flask, slowly pour off most of the clear medium into a bleach bucket, retaining 5–10 ml of medium; gently resuspend the cells in the remaining medium, transfer 1.5 ml of the suspension to an Eppendorf tube, and replenish the flask with fresh algal medium (e.g., 150 ml BBM/WH).

steps.title: Pellet cells by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the Eppendorf tubes at 5,000 rpm for 1 minute, carefully remove the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 ml fresh medium by brief vortexing, spin at 2,500 rpm for 30 seconds, remove supernatant, resuspend again in 1 ml fresh medium, then spin at 5,000 rpm for 1 minute 30 seconds and discard the final supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Recover pellet and grind tissue
steps.instruction: Add just enough medium (≈100 µl) to the pellet, transfer it to a pre‑cooled mortar, grind the cells with liquid nitrogen (six rounds of LN grinding followed by five freeze‑thaw cycles), then transfer the powdered tissue to a clean Eppendorf tube containing 100 µl of extraction‑buffer mix.

substeps.instruction: Alternative grinding: add autoclaved silica sand or zirconium beads (one scoop) to the pellet, grind with a mini‑pestle or vortex adapter (≈1 minute), optionally add a little CTAB to aid grinding; after grinding, let the mixture stand 5 minutes then heat‑block for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: In a hood, prepare a fresh CTAB/β‑mercaptoethanol buffer (2–4 % β‑mercaptoethanol) by mixing the following volumes (choose one scale): 490 µl CTAB + 10 µl β‑mercaptoethanol (2 %); 4,900 µl CTAB + 100 µl β‑mercaptoethanol; or 9,800 µl CTAB + 200 µl β‑mercaptoethanol. Invert to mix. (Commercial CTAB may be used; recipe is in the appendix.)

steps.title: Add extraction buffer and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl of the freshly prepared extraction buffer to each tube (total volume 600 µl, including the 100 µl added earlier) and incubate at 55–60 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Perform chloroform‑phenol extraction
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl of Chloroform:Phenol:Isoamyl alcohol, mix to form an emulsion by pipetting, shaking, or vortexing; for very dirty samples, place tubes on an orbital shaker for 10–30 minutes. Centrifuge 10 minutes at maximum speed (13,000–15,000 rpm).

steps.title: Recover aqueous phase and treat with RNase A
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, carefully pipette off the top aqueous phase into a new labeled 1.5 ml tube, add 4 µl RNase A (1 mg ml⁻¹), invert to mix, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes. Repeat the chloroform‑phenol extraction (steps 6–7) a second time, centrifuging for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with sodium acetate and isopropanol
steps.instruction: Estimate the aqueous volume (~450 µl). Add 0.1 volume of cold 3 M sodium acetate (final 0.3 M; e.g., 45 µl for 450 µl) and then add 0.7–0.9 volumes cold molecular‑grade isopropanol (≈400 µl for 500 µl CTAB). Mix well and let sit in a freezer for 45 minutes to 1 hour (overnight optional). Centrifuge 5 minutes at maximum speed.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, add 700 µl cold 70 % ethanol, invert once to mix, centrifuge 1 minute at maximum speed, remove the liquid, and repeat the ethanol wash once more. If any ethanol remains, leave it rather than disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the pellet by inverting the tubes on a clean paper towel, then resuspend in 45 µl TE buffer. Allow the DNA to dissolve for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C before downstream use.
